chapters.heading: Chapter 1: Enterprise Technology Architecture & Core Infrastructure

content.text: This chapter provides a complete map of Meridian Wealth Advisors' enterprise technology environment—every server, cloud service, network component, and foundational system on which all wealth management tools operate. Understanding this architecture is essential for troubleshooting, capacity planning, vendor negotiations, and regulatory examinations.

Meridian operates a hybrid cloud architecture combining on-premises infrastructure (for latency-sensitive trading and regulatory data retention) with multi-cloud services (AWS and Microsoft Azure) for scalability, disaster recovery, and modern SaaS application hosting. The architecture follows a defense-in-depth security model with network segmentation, zero-trust access controls, and continuous monitoring.

Orion Trading's rebalancing engine is configured with Meridian-specific rules that govern when and how portfolios are rebalanced, incorporating tax awareness, cash management, and compliance constraints.

rows.Setting: 5% relative drift from target allocation at asset class level
rows.Rationale: Balances transaction costs against tracking error; 5% is industry standard for balanced portfolios
rows.Override Conditions: Manual override for accounts with >$50K tax impact; tighter 3% threshold for institutional accounts

rows.Rationale: Avoids uneconomic small trades; reduces custodian ticket charges
rows.Override Conditions: Waived for complete liquidations, tax-loss harvesting, or model changes

rows.Setting: Enabled for all taxable accounts; $1,000 minimum loss threshold
rows.Rationale: Systematic TLH across all eligible accounts; losses offset gains and up to $3,000 ordinary income
rows.Override Conditions: Disabled for accounts with wash-sale risk from held-away accounts; disabled during December wash-sale window (Dec 1–31 for sales, Jan 1–30 for repurchases)

rows.Setting: 30-day hold on repurchasing substantially identical securities across all accounts in household
rows.Rationale: IRS wash-sale rule compliance across all custodians and account types
rows.Override Conditions: No override permitted — hard compliance rule

rows.Setting: 2% cash target for taxable accounts; 1% for retirement accounts
rows.Rationale: Ensures sufficient cash for fee billing, distributions, and management fees without forced liquidation
rows.Override Conditions: Higher cash buffers for accounts with known upcoming distributions; zero cash for fully invested strategies

rows.Setting: Annual realized gain limit per account set collaboratively with client (default: $0 for taxable accounts unless client approves)
rows.Rationale: Prevents unexpected tax bills; aligns trading activity with client's tax situation and expectations
rows.Override Conditions: Unlimited gain budget for tax-exempt accounts (IRAs, Roth); overridden by model changes or client-directed liquidations

rows.Setting: SEC-restricted list (employee trading); client-specific restrictions (ESG exclusions, employer stock limitations)
rows.Rationale: Legal compliance for employee personal trading; alignment with client values and employment restrictions
rows.Override Conditions: Updated monthly by compliance; client-specific restrictions updated at onboarding and annual review

rows.Setting: Pro-rata allocation based on account order size; partial fills distributed proportionally
rows.Rationale: Fair allocation across all accounts per SEC/FINRA guidance; no preferential allocation

rows.Setting: Continuous monitoring with quarterly full rebalance; event-driven rebalancing for cash flows >$25,000
rows.Rationale: Combines systematic discipline with responsiveness to significant cash movements
rows.Override Conditions: Immediate rebalancing for new accounts, model changes, or Investment Committee tactical shifts

chapters.heading: Chapter 15: Disaster Recovery, Business Continuity & Backup

content.text: Meridian maintains enterprise-grade disaster recovery and business continuity capabilities ensuring minimal downtime in the event of infrastructure failures, cyber attacks, or natural disasters. RTO and RPO targets vary by system criticality, with mission-critical systems achieving 1-2 hour RTOs and 10-15 minute RPOs.

Business Impact Analysis (BIA) classifies all systems by recovery priority, maximum tolerable downtime, and data loss impact. Mission-critical systems support 24/7 operations and require RPO ≤ 15 minutes; critical systems must recover within 4 hours; important systems can tolerate 24-hour outages.
Table 15.1.1: Business Impact Analysis (BIA)
▌ ANNUAL REVIEW: BIA is reviewed annually during disaster recovery planning cycle. RTOs are validated through quarterly DR tests where systems are actually recovered to measure real downtime.

Meridian operates a geographically distributed disaster recovery infrastructure with primary production datacenter in New York and secondary DR site in New Jersey, 50 miles distant. Critical systems replicate synchronously (RPO=0) while non-critical systems use asynchronous replication.

Primary Production Site (New York): 1,200 sq ft, 15 cabinets, 120 servers, dual power feeds from separate utility substations, 10 Gbps redundant internet connectivity. Secondary DR Site (New Jersey): 800 sq ft, 10 cabinets, 80 servers (standby), single power feed, 5 Gbps internet. Quarterly DR tests exercise failover of critical applications with recovery time measurements and post-test validation.

items: DR Site Configuration: Active-Passive for databases; synchronous replication using Always-On SQL Server availability groups; warm standby for application servers; automated database failover with <5 minute cutover

Comprehensive glossary defining 40+ technical terms, financial concepts, and regulatory acronyms used throughout this knowledge base.
AUM: Assets Under Management - total client assets managed by Meridian
API: Application Programming Interface - standardized method for systems to communicate
RTO: Recovery Time Objective - maximum acceptable time to restore a system after failure
RPO: Recovery Point Objective - maximum acceptable amount of data loss (time since last backup)
SLA: Service Level Agreement - contractual commitment between vendor and customer on performance
MTPD: Mean Time to Perform Duties - average time to restore business processes after failure
CUSIP: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures - unique security identifier
EOD: End of Day - market closing time (typically 4 PM ET for US markets)
ETL: Extract-Transform-Load - data integration process extracting from sources, transforming, loading to target
ELT: Extract-Load-Transform - alternative approach where transformation occurs post-load in target system
SFTP: SSH File Transfer Protocol - secure method for transferring files over encrypted connection
MFT: Managed File Transfer - enterprise solution for file exchange with encryption and audit logging
DLQ: Dead Letter Queue - queue for messages that cannot be processed normally
SIEM: Security Information and Event Management - platform for log aggregation and security monitoring
SOX: Sarbanes-Oxley - US regulation requiring financial controls and audit trail documentation
KYC: Know Your Customer - regulatory requirement to verify client identity and beneficial ownership
OWASP: Open Web Application Security Project - standards for secure application development
CI/CD: Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment - automated testing and deployment pipeline
IaC: Infrastructure as Code - managing infrastructure through version-controlled code (Terraform, CloudFormation)
HA: High Availability - system design to minimize downtime through redundancy
DR: Disaster Recovery - processes and systems enabling recovery from catastrophic failures
BC: Business Continuity - broader set of procedures ensuring business operations continue during disruptions
DW: Data Warehouse - centralized repository for analytical data (separate from operational databases)
BI: Business Intelligence - analytics, reporting, and visualization of business data
CMDB: Configuration Management Database - repository of all IT assets and their relationships
CAB: Change Advisory Board - governance body reviewing and approving system changes
QA: Quality Assurance - processes and testing to ensure quality of software and systems
UAT: User Acceptance Testing - final testing phase by business users before production deployment
CSS: Cascading Style Sheets - styling markup language for web applications
REST: Representational State Transfer - architectural style for web APIs using HTTP methods
JSON: JavaScript Object Notation - lightweight data interchange format
XML: Extensible Markup Language - markup language for structured data exchange
SWIFT: Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication - messaging standard for financial transactions
FIX: Financial Information eXchange - standardized protocol for real-time securities trading
ACH: Automated Clearing House - US system for electronic funds transfers
XBRL: eXtensible Business Reporting Language - standard for financial reporting to regulators
BGP: Border Gateway Protocol - routing protocol directing internet traffic across networks
VPN: Virtual Private Network - encrypted network tunnel for secure remote connectivity
TLS: Transport Layer Security - encryption protocol (replaces SSL) for securing network communications
OAuth: Open Authorization - framework for delegated authentication without sharing passwords
